architecture.mechanism: Transformer-based fine-tuned language model (CT-BERT) classification of unstructured textual signals to detect anomalous/informative patterns via learned contextual embeddings.
architecture.intervention: Install an onboard NLP classifier (transformer-based, fine-tuned on Hyundai drivetrain telemetry corpora) that ingests CAN-bus time-series messages, DTC-free sensor streams, and transmission solenoid PWM logs to flag anomalous "loss of acceleration with RPM revving" signatures and adaptively adjust transmission control module shift maps and torque converter clutch engagement in real time.
architecture.expected_effect: Earlier detection of slipping/shuddering events absent dashboard MIL illumination, with adaptive TCM recalibration that suppresses the abnormal RPM flare and restores smooth acceleration.
architecture.falsification_test: On a dyno and road-test fleet of 2020 Elantra units exhibiting the documented symptom, compare vehicles with the CT-BERT-style adaptive TCM intervention versus stock TCM across 500 acceleration events; the intervention must reduce RPM-revving magnitude (>500 rpm above commanded) by ≥70% and eliminate driveline shudder in ≥90% of cases (p<0.05 vs. control) with no new DTCs set.
